items.q: Adult nephrotic syndrome is summarized as proteinuria with urine PCR ≥3000 mg/d together with:
items.exp: Proteinuria (urine PCR ≥3000 mg/d); edema; hypoalbuminemia. (Book p761)

items.q: The m/c cause of adult nephrotic syndrome in the cause list is:
items.exp: Causes: membranous nephropathy (m/c); FSGS; MCD (15%); IgA; MPGN; 2° amyloidosis. (Book p761)

items.q: The adult causes grouped under the 'Rare' bracket are:
items.exp: Rare bracket: membrano proliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN), 2° amyloidosis. (Book p761)

items.q: The adult management sequence is biopsy first, then:
opts: Rule out 2° causes such as paraneoplastic syndrome
items.exp: Management: 1. biopsy; 2. rule out 2° causes (Eg: paraneoplastic syndrome). (Book p761)

items.q: The adult steroid trial written is 1 mg/kg/d for:
items.exp: Steroid: 1 mg/kg/d × 4 months; no response → SRNS. (Book p761)

items.q: An adult failing the 4-month steroid course is labelled SRNS, whose m/c cause is:
The note's Maltese crosses in polarized light and oval fat bodies are both annotated as seen in:
items.exp: Maltese crosses in polarized light and oval fat bodies: seen in Fabry's disease. (Book p761)
